content: 1. Both siponimod and moxifloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 2. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the absorption of moxifloxacin in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize this effect, separate their administration by at least 2 hours or consider alternative treatments. 3. Sodium citrate/citric acid also decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to oral formulations. Separate administration by 2 hours or use alternative drugs. 4. Strontium ranelate reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The combination is contraindicated, and strontium ranelate should be suspended during antibiotic therapy. 5. Sunitinib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 6. Tacrolimus and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. 7. Tetrabenazine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative medications. 8. Thioridazine and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or consider alternative treatments. 9. Trazodone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 10. Moxifloxacin and tretinoin (oral or topical) may increase phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid their combined use or consider alternative treatments. 11. Trifluoperazine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 12. Trimipramine and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or consider alternative therapies. 13. Moxifloxacin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Administer the vaccine only after completing antibiotic therapy. 14. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Extreme caution is advised when combining vilanterol with QTc-prolonging agents due to potential cardiovascular effects. 15. Moxifloxacin and vandetanib both increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If necessary, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 16. Vemurafenib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or consider alternative therapies. 17. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when combining vilanterol with QTc-prolonging agents due to potential cardiovascular effects. 18. Vorinostat and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or consider alternative treatments. 19. Moxifloxacin and ziprasidone both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 20. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 21. Albuterol and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Moxifloxacin and alfuzosin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Moxifloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine, potentially leading to seizures. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Amifampridine lowers the seizure threshold, and coadministration with other seizure-lowering drugs increases this risk. 24. Arformoterol and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Azithromycin and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Moxifloxacin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 28. Betamethasone and moxifloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Calcium acetate reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 30. Calcium carbonate decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 31. Calcium chloride reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 32. Calcium citrate decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 33. Calcium gluconate reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 34. Moxifloxacin and celecoxib increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 35. Chloroquine increases moxifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ciprofloxacin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 37. Moxifloxacin and citalopram both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 38. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Coadministration of corticotropin and moxifloxacin increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Coadministration of cortisone and moxifloxacin increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Crizotinib and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 42. Dasatinib and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Moxifloxacin and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not clinically prolong the QT interval, but certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 44. Dexamethasone and moxifloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Dichlorphenamide and moxifloxacin both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Moxifloxacin and diclofenac increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but an additional form of birth control may be advisable. 48. Moxifloxacin and diflunisal increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Moxifloxacin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Dolasetron and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Escitalopram and moxifloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 54. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Moxifloxacin decreases the effects of ethosuximide by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. There are also case reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. 57. Moxifloxacin and etodolac increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 58. Etrasimod and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction when initiated, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes when combined with QT-prolonging drugs. 59. Ezogabine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses of 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is combined with QT-prolonging agents. 60. Fennel reduces moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Moxifloxacin and fenoprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Ferric citrate reduces moxifloxacin levels by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer moxifloxacin at least 2 hours before or after ferric citrate. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Flecainide and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 64. Fludrocortisone and moxifloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Fluoxetine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 66. Moxifloxacin and flurbiprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 67. Fluvoxamine and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 68. Foscarnet and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 69. Moxifloxacin decreases the effects of fosphenytoin by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. There are also case reports of quinolones increasing phenytoin levels. 70. Moxifloxacin and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 71. Gadobenate and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 72. Moxifloxacin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Gepirone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 74. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of glimepiride through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 75. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of glipizide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 76. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of glyburide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 77. Goserelin increases moxifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 78. Histrelin increases moxifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 79. Hydrocortisone and moxifloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Hydrocortisone rectal and moxifloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Hydroxyzine increases moxifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 82. Moxifloxacin and ibuprofen increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 83. Moxifloxacin and ibuprofen IV increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 84. Iloperidone and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 85. Indacaterol inhaled and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 86. Moxifloxacin and indomethacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 87. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of insulin aspart through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely. 88. Moxifloxacin enhances the effects of insulin detemir through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia, with gatifloxacin being the most likely to cause dysglycemia and moxifloxacin the least likely.
